text:
kevin: Heads up — we have a customer report that OAuth redirect flows fail intermittently for requests coming through the legacy proxy. Traced it to our rewrite rules: we currently strip duplicate query params and dedupe on key+value, and it looks like `state` sometimes gets dropped when `return_to` is present.

sara: repro steps?

kevin: curl to /auth/start?state=abc123&return_to=/app -> upstream sees only `return_to`. I think our query-normalizer is treating `state` as a duplicate because of ordering and a bug in the comparator.

dilip: we have 2 problems here: (1) query dedupe ordering bug, (2) new request from sales to map `cid` query param -> `x-customer-id` header for legacy clients. That header is also used by rate-limiter to attribute quotas. Need to be careful about precedence and PII.

anna: Agree. Proposals:
- Fix dedupe comparator to preserve first-seen param unless explicitly canonicalized.
- Always preserve OAuth params (state, redirect_uri) in the whitelist.
- Drop common tracking params: utm_*, gclid, fbclid.
- Add a rewrite rule: `if query.has(cid) and route.meta.legacy_proxy then add header x-customer-id = query.cid` with `sensitive: true` so runtime masks it in logs.

marc: for cache-key: don't include cid/header in cache key — we need separate client attribution vs cached response. So add `cache_key.overrides.exclude: ["x-customer-id","cid"]` in route config.

kevin: example of the rule I sketched:
```
- match: /api/*
  rewrites:
    query_normalize:
      dedupe: first_seen
      whitelist: ["state", "redirect_uri"]
      drop_prefixes: ["utm_", "gclid", "fbclid"]
    header_inject:
      - name: "x-customer-id"
        from: query.cid
        condition: route.meta.legacy_proxy == true
        sensitive: true
```

sara: SGTM. A few caveats:
- If `x-customer-id` is present already, we should not overwrite unless `force=true`.
- For private deployments, customers may want to keep cid in logs; make sensitive configurable per-tenant.

dilip: Also: when injecting the header we need to ensure auth delegation rules can't be bypassed. If we map cid from query for client attribution, add an allowlist of routes so it's not used for auth decisions unless route.meta.allows_query_asserted_id.

marc: Test plan:
- Unit tests for dedupe comparator with edge cases: param order inversion, repeated keys with different values.
- Integration test hitting /auth/start with various param orders.
- Canary rollout: enable rule on 5% traffic for legacy-proxy service and monitor `auth.redirect_failures` and `rewrite.header_inject_errors`.

infra-bot: deploy-triggered: rollout config updated by kevin. Can start canary at 2026-03-20T17:00Z via /deploy

kevin: I'll open a spec PR and add e2e. Also adding a telemetry event when we drop params: `rewrite.query_drop` with tags {route, reason}

sara: don't forget to add docs in the console for `sensitive` header flag and cache_key overrides.

anna: one more gotcha — we normalize paths by collapsing `//` sequences and removing trailing slash for static routes, but for OAuth redirect_uri we must preserve exact path. So whitelist redirect endpoints from path normalization.

kevin: I'll include all those in the PR. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

sara: lgtm, please add a migration note for dedicated/private customers who may have relied on old dedupe behavior.

kevin: filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4923

dilip: nice. Assigned to anna for review and marc for tests.

anna: I'll take it.

marc: I'll add canary dashboards: `rewrite_errors`, `redirect_failures`, `header_inject_rate`.

kevin: closing loop — once PR merges, we'll run canary and then rollout 50% -> 100%.
